components.name: Cloud SQL Postgres (aforo-pg)
components.what: One shared Postgres 17 instance with one database and one user per service (catalog, orders, inventory). Started and stopped by the env_on switch.
components.serves: Durable state of catalog, orders and inventory (each in its own logical DB: db-catalog, db-orders, db-inventory), including their outbox/inbox/idempotency tables.

why.note: db-f1-micro allows 25 connections (22 usable); instance caps x DB_POOL_MAX are budgeted to 19 of 22.
activation_policy follows env_on (ALWAYS/NEVER), changed only through make up/down.
Stopped instance bills disk only, so dev costs close to nothing when off.

gcp.name: aforo-pg (aforo-dev-teamf:southamerica-east1:aforo-pg)
gcp.config: POSTGRES_17, db-f1-micro, ENTERPRISE edition, ZONAL, 10 GB PD_HDD no autoresize, no backups, max_connections=25, public IPv4 with ssl_mode ENCRYPTED_ONLY and no authorized networks; services connect via the Cloud SQL connector socket mounted at /cloudsql (roles/cloudsql.client on catalog/orders/inventory runtime SAs). DATABASE_URL per service from Secret Manager aforo-<svc>-database-url.

components.name: Memorystore for Redis (aforo-queue)
components.what: Redis 7.2, BASIC tier, 1 GB, private IP via DIRECT_PEERING on aforo-vpc. Exists only while redis_enabled = true.
components.serves: Queue positions, admission state and pass data for the waiting room; also the Gateway's per-IP rate-limit counters (ADR-0001 amendment).

why.note: Cloud Run has no TCP ingress, so D-15 (Redis on Cloud Run) was replaced by Memorystore created only for live tests and demos.
Superseded by ADR-0001.
Bills by provisioned capacity (~US$1-2/day), so it is created by IaC only for windows.

gcp.name: aforo-queue
gcp.config: BASIC, 1 GB, REDIS_7_2, DIRECT_PEERING to aforo-vpc, no AUTH, no TLS. REDIS_URL (redis://host:port, empty when off) passed by Terraform to queue and gateway, both with Direct VPC egress PRIVATE_RANGES_ONLY.

components.name: Secret Manager secrets

components.name: Service accounts and invoker IAM
components.what: One runtime SA per Cloud Run service/function (aforo-<name>-run) plus caller SAs aforo-pubsub-push, aforo-tasks-invoker, aforo-scheduler, aforo-eventarc, aforo-functions-build, and github-ci for CI via Workload Identity Federation.
components.serves: Decides who can invoke whom: only web and gateway are public; every other service/function is private and invoked with Google OIDC ID tokens using custom audiences aforo-<svc>.

why.note: IAM is Terraform-owned configuration.
prewarmer gets run.developer only on aforo-gateway and aforo-queue plus actAs on their runtime SAs.
Logic services trust gateway headers because only gateway (and system SAs) can invoke them.

components.name: Terraform (infra/envs/dev)

components.name: Makefile runtime switches

components.name: Structured JSON logs and correlation ID
components.what: One JSON line per request (severity, message, service, correlationId, userId, route, status, latencyMs) written to stdout/stderr by @aforo/common, indexed by Cloud Logging as jsonPayload.
components.serves: Lets one purchase be followed across gateway, services, Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks and functions by a single correlationId.

why.note: Traceability tactic: correlationId in every log line, envelope field and Pub/Sub attribute.

gcp.name: jsonPayload.*
gcp.config: No custom sinks; ERROR/CRITICAL to stderr, rest to stdout. Gateway generates X-Correlation-Id (UUID v4) if absent; AsyncLocalStorage carries it; Pub/Sub consumers adopt it from the envelope.

components.observed: Happy path step 10: correlationId ecd0fae3-... followed across orders, inventory and gateway, and the bus hop catalog->inventory (docs/evidence/happy-path/README.md). E-05 poison fe16d541-... traced through 3 consumers and dlq-monitor.
gotchas: Never log tokens, secrets or full bodies; log queuePass when X-Queue-Pass is present.
Invalid incoming correlation IDs (not UUID v4) are replaced with a new one.

components.name: Dead-letter alert
components.what: Log-based metric aforo/dead_letters counting jsonPayload.event="dead_letter" lines from aforo-dlq-monitor, an alert policy 'aforo: message dead-lettered' (count > 0 over 60 s, auto_close 1800 s) and email notification channels from var.alert_emails.
components.serves: Turns a message reaching any DLQ into an incident and an email within 5 minutes.

why.note: DLQ with messages -> alert tactic.
dlq-monitor emits the structured log the metric counts.
5 delivery attempts, 10-60 s backoff and 60 s alignment keep the loop under 5 min.

gcp.type: Cloud Logging metric + Cloud Monitoring alert policy + email channel
gcp.name: aforo/dead_letters; 'aforo: message dead-lettered'
gcp.config: DELTA INT64 metric; condition ALIGN_COUNT over 60 s, threshold > 0, duration 0 s; documentation points to docs/runbooks/demo.md (E-05). One email address in alert_emails.
gcp.state: logging metrics list: aforo/dead_letters. Alert policy enabled with 1 notification channel.

components.name: Contracts (OpenAPI, events, conventions)
components.what: OpenAPI files per service and function, event envelope and payload JSON Schemas, and normative cross-service conventions. The contract wins over code and READMEs.
components.serves: Single source of truth for routes, headers, errors, formats and messaging; Prism mocks and Redocly lint run from it.

why.note: Breaking change creates /v2, never edits /v1.
Idempotency-Key replays return the same body and status.
Schema violations are 422 VALIDATION_ERROR; 400 only for unparseable bodies and invalid envelopes.
POST /internal/v1/housekeeping on catalog, inventory, orders.

gotchas: contracts/README.md still says 'Status: DRAFT - to be frozen Tue Sept 29' with open points listed.
Conventions say the caller requests an ID token 'for the target URL'; infra and CI use custom audiences aforo-<svc> instead.

Key rules: /api/v1 public, /internal/v1 not exposed by gateway; errors application/problem+json with type https://aforo.dev/errors/<code>; money integer cents + COP; ISO-8601 UTC; UUID v4; Idempotency-Key with Idempotent-Replayed header and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; envelope {messageId,type,version,occurredAt,correlationId,producer,data} with type and correlationId also as Pub/Sub attributes.
